free_tier.stated: No English signup credit is published. The pricing FAQ carries only a conditional example: 'For example, if you received a $100 credit for 60 days'. The surviving $100 statement is Japanese-locale meta text on akamai.com/ja/lp/free-trial, and /lp/free-credit-trial/ returns 404 with no archive capture.

record.interface_detail: Access interface not documented in published terms.

limits.value: hourly or monthly billing across Dedicated, Shared and High Memory plans; the page does not restate the rates
outbound transfer is included per plan, from 0 to 20 TB a month depending on family; G8 and GPU plans bundle differently

identity_cost.detail: card required on file; a USD 1 authorisation hold may be placed by the bank when the processor verifies the card; debit accepted; prepaid is not stated on the vendor's own payment page

record.confidence_note: the pricing pages and the Japanese trial page were read on 2026-10-23; the English $100 offer does not exist as a page | Payment facts re-read on 2026-10-24: the card types, the hold and the identity gate each come from a first-party page quoted in evidence[].

evidence.proved: quoted: Nanode 1 GB $5.00/mo $0.0075/hr; Linode 2 GB $12.00/mo $0.0180/hr; Linode 4 GB $24.00/mo $0.0360/hr
301 to akamai.com/cloud/pricing; no credit on the plan tables
meta description only: '$100 相当の無料クレジット'; the English path is 404
quoted: 'Credit card. Pay using all popular credit (and debit) cards, including those issued by Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express, and UnionPay.'
quoted, the hold: 'When the payment processor verifies your credit card, your bank may place a $1 authorization hold on your account.'

record.notes: The $100 for 60 days cannot be ranked because no English page states it as an offer. A card is mandatory for every account, whether or not a credit is granted. Debit and the USD 1 hold are documented on the vendor's own payment-methods page. Prepaid is deliberately recorded as not stated: a Linode community answer says prepaid cards are accepted, but that is a third-party statement on a forum and no first-party page read says it.

session_cap.note: an instance bills while it exists; the page states no reap

extras.price_note: a VPS bills by the month with an hourly rate capped at the monthly figure, so the two columns answer two questions: destroying the box between runs versus keeping it up.
extras.price_basis: 10 h/day column = 300 h at the hourly rate, which is what a server destroyed between runs costs; 24/7 column = the monthly cap, because a VPS kept up all month stops at the cap. Rates re-read on the vendor pricing page on 2026-10-23.

ps.price: SSD-backed persistent volumes, priced per gigabyte

net.allowance: 0 to 20 TB a month included depending on plan family

payment_methods.identity: email, username and password; card on file

card.category: L4 anycast and GRE DDoS protection
card.summary: No free tier is published; both the routed and the anycast shapes are contract products.

record.category: L4 anycast and GRE DDoS protection

free_tier.stated: No free tier is published; both the routed and the anycast shapes are contract products.

egress.terms: No volume is published. The service is sold as capacity against an attack profile, not as a byte allowance.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.interface_detail: Prolexic IP Protect Configuration API on techdocs.akamai.com/ip-protect, managing mapped IP addresses and policy domains
record.tooling: Prolexic IP Protect Configuration API; otherwise a managed service
record.chaining: IP Protect is the only path that works with a single free VM as origin, and it needs a contract, so it does not chain with anything free

limits.value: Routed GRE requires an assigned /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), BGP advertisement and GRE support; the alternative is a contract for IP Protect

record.binding_note: The block size and the contract are the gates, not bytes. A client with one rented VM and no prefix can only take the IP Protect shape, which is the anycast product and is still contracted.

identity_cost.detail: A contract; the routed option additionally needs an assigned /24 or larger advertisable block, the ability to advertise via BGP, and GRE support on the origin network hardware.

record.reliability_note: the GRE shape is only for networks that can announce their own prefix; the anycast shape is the only one open to a host without a /24
record.confidence_note: The /24-BGP-GRE requirement and the IP Protect anycast alternative are quoted from the page read. The IP Protect price, its protocol coverage and its port model are not published and were not read.

evidence.proved: For the Prolexic Routed GRE option, you need to have an assigned /24 or larger advertisable network block (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), the ability to advertise your network traffic via BGP, and support generic routing encapsulation (GRE) with your origin-based network hardware.

For customers with less than a routable IPv4 /24 and/or IPv6 /48, fragmented IP space, or cloud-hosting provider, the Prolexic IP Protect option provides the same level of DDoS protection via IP anycast to route symmetric traffic through Akamai scrubbing centers.

record.notes: The useful sentence on this page is the one that names the exact situation: 'less than a routable IPv4 /24 ... or cloud-hosting provider'. IP Protect is therefore the only Akamai shape that could apply, and it is contracted. techdocs.akamai.com/ip-protect exists as a configuration API but the welcome page 404s; the API index was reachable and describes mapped IP addresses.

extras.wg_detail: Prolexic IP Protect routes symmetric traffic through Akamai scrubbing centres by IP anycast, which carries any UDP listener on that address; the routed option uses GRE instead.
extras.volume_stated: No volume is published. The service is sold as capacity against an attack profile, not as a byte allowance.
extras.transit_note: clean traffic is delivered from Akamai scrubbing centres to the origin

free_tier.stated: "Both EdgeWorkers and EdgeKV offer a free pricing tier that enables the full feature list of the product and includes a total of 60 million free events (30 million per product) per month." The access rule: the Evaluation tier needs an existing Akamai contract, and without one the only route is a free trial that Akamai approves.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: Nothing without a contract. The 60 million events are real but sit behind a sales relationship, which is the same class as an institutional quota.

limits.value: The 60 million events a month is gated on an approval: the Evaluation tier requires an active Akamai contract and Control Center credentials, and the alternative trial is granted by Akamai after a manual sign-up review.

record.limits_note: The 60 million events a month is gated on an approval: the Evaluation tier requires an active Akamai contract and Control Center credentials, and the alternative trial is granted by Akamai after a manual sign-up review.
record.binding_note: The 60 million events a month is gated on an approval: the Evaluation tier requires an active Akamai contract and Control Center credentials, and the alternative trial is granted by Akamai after a manual sign-up review.

identity_cost.detail: institution: 'If you have an active Akamai contract and login credentials for Akamai Control Center you can use these instructions to sign up for the EdgeWorkers Evaluation tier', and without a contract the route is a trial request 'Akamai must approve', with a delivery product such as ION as a prerequisite. No card, hold, phone number or ID document appears in any evidence row: unknown. The previous kind, card, was not supported by the record's evidence.

evidence.proved: "If you have an active Akamai contract and login credentials for Akamai Control Center you can use these instructions to sign up for the EdgeWorkers Evaluation tier", and the tier has no time limit, quoted
without a contract the route is a trial request that Akamai must approve, and a delivery product such as ION is a prerequisite
vendor press release states the free tier totals 60 million free events a month, 30 million per product

record.notes: Classified as fails-identity because the unlimited-time tier needs an existing commercial account, and the reachable substitute is an approval-gated trial. This is the highest headline number in the edge class that is not actually reachable on an email alone, and it is the reason not to put Akamai beside Deno and Val Town in a table.
